code_actions.rationale: Record documents gallstone (biliary) etiology and infected necrosis (CT impression, GI consult, H&P problem list); idiopathic/uninfected pancreatitis (K85.01) is not supported.
Biliary (gallstone) etiology with infected pancreatic necrosis is documented; recode to biliary acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis (sequence as principal diagnosis).

K85.82 (other acute pancreatitis w/ infected necrosis) duplicates/duplicates etiology; gallstone-specific infected necrosis is documented and should be represented by the biliary-infected code instead.
No documentation of diverticulitis with perforation/abscess appears among the admission/discharge problem lists or hospital course (discharge diagnoses do not include diverticulitis).

Provider-identified Klebsiella pneumoniae as the causative organism of infected pancreatic necrosis/sepsis; use organism-specific sepsis code A41.53 and mark POA=Y. The separate B96.1 organism-specifier is redundant when A41.53 is used.
Organism (Klebsiella pneumoniae) is documented but is embedded in the organism-specific sepsis code (A41.53); B96.1 is redundant and should be removed.
ARDS is documented in initial critical care documentation and resolved by discharge; POA should be Y rather than billed N.

Operative/procedure documentation describes video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) via existing drain tract and drainage/debridement rather than percutaneous excision of the pancreas; 0FBG3ZZ (excision) is not supported.

No clear documentation of separate peritoneal cavity drainage is present; procedure notes describe retroperitoneal drainage/debridement and percutaneous pancreatic drainage rather than peritoneal cavity drainage.

evidence.quote: Impression Severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis.
Video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement performed via existing drain tract. Additional necrotic pancreatic tissue removed. Drain replaced with larger caliber. Adequate drainage achieved.

VS: Tmax 39.4C | HR 126 | MAP 66 | RR 29 | SpO2 88%. Airway: orally intubated, mechanically ventilated. Gen: Sedated, critically ill; RASS -4; not responsive to voice. HEENT: MMM; no scleral icterus. Cor: Tachy; RRR; no M/R/G; extremities cool; vasopressors on.

The course was complicated by ARDS with successful prone positioning, AKI managed conservatively, transient abdominal compartment concerns managed non-operatively, infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16
2 Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae
Extubation was successful on ICU day 18 following resolution of ARDS.
Abdomen: soft, non-distended, +bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry.
Hemodynamically on norepinephrine for septic and pancreatitis-related shock.
Vitals: continuous telemetry, arterial-line BP, SpO2, PA catheter monitoring; hourly assessment; strict I/O; intra-abdominal pressure monitoring.

system_note: What was billed: claim MR_22 listed multiple, overlapping pancreatitis diagnoses (K85.01 idiopathic w/ uninfected necrosis; K85.11 biliary w/ uninfected necrosis; K85.82 other acute pancreatitis w/ infected necrosis), organism-level and nonspecific sepsis codes (A41.50 + B96.1), R65.21 severe sepsis w/ septic shock, ARDS (J80, POA=N billed), and an ICD-10-PCS 'Excision of pancreas' (0FBG3ZZ). What the record documents and why it disagrees with the billing: 1) Etiology and necrosis status: imaging and consults document gallstone (biliary) etiology with infected pancreatic necrosis (not idiopathic or uninfected necrosis) — CT Impression: Severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n13, Impression). Gastroenterology explicitly: Severe pancreatitis by revised Atlanta criteria; gallstone etiology confirmed (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n12, p.346). The H&P active problem list also records infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n9, Active Problem List). Conclusion: K85.01 (idiopathic) and K85.11 (biliary w/ uninfected necrosis) are not supported simultaneously with documented infected, gallstone pancreatitis — the correct principal pancreatitis code should reflect biliary etiology with infected necrosis (recode K85.11 to K85.81 and remove K85.01 and K85.82). (evidence: ev_0001, ev_0005) 2) Sepsis organism and sequencing/POA: the record documents Klebsiella as the infecting organism and documents clinical sepsis/septic shock with vasopressor use and elevated lactate. The discharge course documents infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and step-up drainage then VARD (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n1198, Hospital Course). The initial ICU notes show intubation, vasopressors on, and lactate 4.9 mmol/L (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n11, p.363) and nursing notes document norepinephrine for septic and pancreatitis-related shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n10). Therefore A41.50 (gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) should be specified to the Klebsiella sepsis code (A41.53) and the B96.1 organism code is redundant when A41.53 is used; POA indicators should reflect sepsis present on admission (evidence: ev_0004, ev_0003, ev_0008). 3) ARDS POA miscoding: ARDS is documented in the inpatient record and discharge summary as part of the initial critical illness (record header and progress notes list ARDS; the discharge summary documents resolved ARDS and successful extubation), so J80 should be POA=Y rather than POA=N as billed (evidence: ev_0001, ev_0006). 4) Procedure/technique mismatch (wrong ICD-10-PCS): billed 0FBG3ZZ Excision of pancreas (percutaneous) is not supported — operative/procedure documentation describes a video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) performed via existing drain tract with additional necrotic tissue removed and drain replacement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n109, Procedure Note - VARD). The correct action is to remove the excision code and retain the drainage/debridement/drain codes actually performed. Additionally, 0W9G3ZZ (drainage of peritoneal cavity) is not supported by the documentation of retroperitoneal drainage/debridement and percutaneous pancreatic drainage. (evidence: ev_0002, ev_0004) 5) Procedures supported in the record: CT-guided percutaneous drainage and post-VARD CT and procedure notes support percutaneous drainage (0F9G30Z) and VARD (procedure description supports drainage/debridement, not excision) and the discharge summary documents PICC and PEG site presence (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n1198). Extubation on ICU day 18 confirms prolonged mechanical ventilation (>96 hours) supporting 5A1D90Z (evidence: ev_0004, ev_0006). Summary/impact: multiple billed entries are inconsistent with the medical record (duplicate/misclassified pancreatitis codes, redundant organism code plus unspecified sepsis code, unsupported pancreas excision PCS code, incorrect POA on ARDS/A41.50). Code changes applied in this determination include: remove K85.01; recode K85.11 to K85.81 (principal); remove K85.82; remove K57.21; recode A41.50 to A41.53 and mark POA=Y; remove B96.1; keep J80 but correct POA to Y; remove 0FBG3ZZ; remove 0W9G3ZZ. See evidence_cited entries below for the specific supporting passages and the code_decisions section for the full, claim-level corrected code set and the reasoning for each change.
rationale_letter:
Date: [date of determination]
To: Billing/Coding Department, Lake Ontario Regional Medical Center
Re: DRG Audit — Claim MR_22 (Admission 2026-08-25 to 2027-01-13)
Dear Provider,
We completed a DRG-level audit of claim MR_22. After three-way review of the billed codes, the medical record, and applicable coding policy, we have found inaccuracies requiring correction.
Finding: Multiple diagnoses and procedures are miscoded or unsupported as billed. Specifically: (1) The record documents severe necrotizing gallstone (biliary) pancreatitis with infected pancreatic necrosis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae (CT impression and GI consult), not idiopathic or uninfected necrosis. Therefore, the billed K85.01 (idiopathic) and K85.11 (biliary with uninfected necrosis) are not supported concurrently and must be corrected to the biliary-infected necrosis code (K85.81) as the principal diagnosis; K85.82 (other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) is also removed as it duplicates the biliary-specific infected necrosis representation. (2) The sepsis coding should specify Klebsiella sepsis rather than nonspecific gram-negative sepsis with a separate organism code; documentation shows Klebsiella as the causative organism and clinical septic shock with vasopressors and elevated lactate. Therefore A41.50/B96.1 should be replaced by A41.53 with POA=Y. (3) The PCS procedure 0FBG3ZZ (excision of pancreas) is not supported — the operative record documents video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) via an existing drain tract (drainage/debridement), not an excision; 0W9G3ZZ is likewise unsupported. (4) Present-on-admission flags require correction (e.g., J80 ARDS and organism-specific sepsis are documented on admission).
Basis (selected record citations relied upon):
- CT Abdomen: Impression — Severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis (Diagnostic Imaging Report, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n13, p.384). ev_0001
- Gastroenterology consult: Severe pancreatitis by revised Atlanta criteria; gallstone etiology confirmed (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n12, p.346). - Active Problem List / H&P: 2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae (History & Physical, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n9, p.241). ev_0005
- ICU documentation: mechanical ventilation, vasopressors on, ABG/lactate 4.9 mmol/L indicating shock physiology (Critical Care Progress Note, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n11, p.363). ev_0003
- Discharge summary / hospital course: infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem; CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 and video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16 (Discharge/Transfer Summary, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n1198, p.1042). ev_0004
- Procedure note (VARD): Video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement performed via existing drain tract. Additional necrotic pancreatic tissue removed. Drain replaced with larger caliber. Adequate drainage achieved (Procedure Note - VARD, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_22.pdf-n109, p.817). ev_0002
Corrections required: The claim will be adjusted to (a) remove K85.01 and recode K85.11 to K85.81 and remove K85.82 (sequence K85.81 as principal); (b) replace A41.50/B96.1 with the organism-specific sepsis code (A41.53) and mark sepsis POA=Y; (c) remove 0FBG3ZZ and 0W9G3ZZ (excision and unsupported peritoneal drainage) and retain percutaneous drainage/debridement/drain codes supported by the procedure notes; (d) remove K57.21 (no documentation of diverticulitis with perforation/abscess); (e) correct POA flags (e.g., J80 POA=Y). The full corrected diagnosis and procedure lists are provided in the audit determination record.
If you disagree with the factual findings above, please provide the specific dated provider documentation (progress note, operative note, microbiology report with interpreted culture and provider attribution, or explicit physician query response) that supports your originally-submitted coding within 30 days.
Sincerely,
[Auditor Name]
Senior Clinical Claims Auditor
